views.name: matches_with_valid_score_and_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "Match"."id" AS id,
  "Match"."league_id" AS league_id,
  "Match"."season" AS season,
  "Match"."home_team_goal" AS home_team_goal,
  "Match"."away_team_goal" AS away_team_goal
FROM "Match"
JOIN "League" ON "Match"."league_id" = "League"."id"
WHERE "Match"."home_team_goal" IS NOT NULL
  AND "Match"."away_team_goal" IS NOT NULL
  AND "Match"."season" IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per match filtered to rows that have non-NULL scores and an explicit season value. Keeps match-level fields needed for scoring, grouping by league, and joining to league.

views.name: league_match_goal_totals_by_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  league_id,
  season,
  SUM(COALESCE(home_team_goal,0) + COALESCE(away_team_goal,0)) AS total_goals
FROM
  matches_with_valid_score_and_season
GROUP BY
  league_id,
  season
views.description: Aggregated match goal totals per league per season. Produces one row per (league_id, season) with the summed raw goals across matches. Does not attach league name, leaving that for a join.

views.name: league_id_to_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  League.id AS id,
  League.name AS name
FROM League
views.description: Canonical lookup of league identifier to league name. One row per League.id with the human-readable name.
validated_on: Give the name of the league with the highest matches of all time and how many matches were played in the said league.

views.name: matches_filtered_by_league_and_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "id",
  "match_api_id",
  "season",
  "league_id",
  "home_team_api_id",
  "away_team_api_id",
  "home_team_goal",
  "away_team_goal",
  "date"
FROM "Match"
views.description: All Match rows with basic match outcome fields; intended as a reusable cohort for matches in any league/season once filters are applied at query time.
validated_on: How many matches were held in the Belgium Jupiler League in April, 2009?
counter_examples: Give the name of the league had the most matches in the 2008/2009 season?

views.name: team_identity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  team_api_id,
  team_long_name,
  team_short_name
FROM Team
views.description: Canonical team identifier table exposing each team's API id and human-readable names for joins and presentation.

views.name: away_win_events_per_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.away_team_api_id AS away_team_api_id,
  CASE
    WHEN m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL
     AND m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL
     AND m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_away_win
FROM matches_filtered_by_league_and_season AS m
views.description: Denormalized match-level rows indicating whether the match was an away win and exposing away team id; useful for counting away wins per team when filtered by league/season.

views.name: team_attributes_nonnull_buildupplayspeed
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  team_api_id,
  team_fifa_api_id,
  date,
  buildUpPlaySpeed,
  buildUpPlaySpeedClass,
  buildUpPlayDribbling,
  buildUpPlayDribblingClass,
  buildUpPlayPassing,
  buildUpPlayPassingClass,
  buildUpPlayPositioningClass
FROM Team_Attributes
WHERE buildUpPlaySpeed IS NOT NULL
views.description: Subset of Team_Attributes rows where buildUpPlaySpeed is present (non-NULL). Keeps team identifiers and all build-up/play metrics for reuse.

views.name: team_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Team.team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  Team.team_fifa_api_id AS team_fifa_api_id,
  Team.team_long_name AS team_long_name,
  Team.team_short_name AS team_short_name,
  Team.id AS id
FROM Team
views.description: Canonical Team lookup with stable identifiers and display name. Normalizes the team identity fields used to join and present team info.

views.name: team_max_buildupplayspeed
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  team_api_id,
  MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed) AS max_buildUpPlaySpeed
FROM
  Team_Attributes
WHERE
  buildUpPlaySpeed IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  team_api_id
views.description: Per-team aggregated measure: the maximum buildUpPlaySpeed observed for each team (from Team_Attributes rows where buildUpPlaySpeed is not NULL).

views.name: match_draw_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  mv.id AS match_id,
  mv.league_id AS league_id,
  mv.season AS season,
  CASE WHEN mv.home_team_goal = mv.away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_draw,
  mv.home_team_goal AS home_team_goal,
  mv.away_team_goal AS away_team_goal
FROM matches_with_valid_score_and_season mv
views.description: One row per Match with a normalized flag indicating whether the match was a draw and canonical season/league identifiers. Keeps raw goal values and exposes season and league for filtering/grouping.

views.name: league_match_counts_by_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.league_id AS league_id,
  m.season AS season,
  COUNT(m.id) AS match_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN m.home_team_goal = m.away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS draw_count
FROM
  matches_with_valid_score_and_season m
GROUP BY
  m.league_id,
  m.season
views.description: Aggregated counts of matches per league per season with counts of draws and total matches. One row per league-season. Useful for quickly answering season-level league comparisons.
counter_examples: Give the name of the league had the most matches in the 2008/2009 season?

views.name: league_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  name
FROM League
views.description: Reference table for leagues exposing league id and canonical league name (one row per League.id).

views.name: player_attributes_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Player_Attributes.id AS id,
  Player_Attributes.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id AS player_fifa_api_id,
  Player_Attributes.date AS date,
  Player_Attributes.sprint_speed AS sprint_speed,
  Player_Attributes.overall_rating AS overall_rating,
  Player_Attributes.potential AS potential,
  Player_Attributes.preferred_foot AS preferred_foot
FROM Player_Attributes
views.description: Row-level Player_Attributes records (one row per Player_Attributes.id) with original columns preserved for filtering and later aggregation. Use this to form cohorts by date ranges, attribute thresholds, and to compute per-player stats within any period.
validated_on: For the players who had a 77 points overall rating on 2016/6/23, who was the oldest? Give the name of the player.

views.name: player_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_api_id,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  player_name,
  birthday,
  height,
  weight
FROM Player
views.description: Canonical Player rows (one row per Player.player_api_id) exposing stable identifiers and personal attributes useful for joins and age computation.
validated_on: Among the players born before the year 1986, how many of them would remain in his position and defense while the team attacked?
For the players who had a 77 points overall rating on 2016/6/23, who was the oldest? Give the name of the player.
counter_examples: What was the overall rating for Aaron Mooy on 2016/2/4?

views.name: player_max_sprint_by_period
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  par.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  MAX(par.sprint_speed) AS max_sprint_speed_in_period,
  COUNT(par.id) AS attribute_row_count_in_period,
  MIN(par.date) AS min_attribute_date_in_period,
  MAX(par.date) AS max_attribute_date_in_period
FROM
  player_attributes_rows par
GROUP BY
  par.player_api_id
views.description: Per-player aggregated measures of sprint_speed (and other selected measures) computed within an arbitrary date window. One row per Player.player_api_id containing the max sprint_speed observed in the window and the count of attribute rows in the window.

views.name: match_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.league_id AS league_id,
  m.match_api_id AS match_api_id,
  -- normalize date text to YYYY-MM-DD (keep time if present)
  substr(m.date, 1, 10) AS date
FROM Match m
WHERE m.league_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical row-level Match records with key identifiers and core dimensions preserved for counting/filters; normalizes date text and exposes league and match identifiers.

views.name: league_with_match_counts_candidate
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  league_id,
  COUNT(*) AS match_count
FROM
  Match
WHERE
  league_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  league_id
views.description: Aggregate match counts per league_id. Produces one row per league_id with the raw match count; does not attach league.name to keep separation of aggregation and lookup.

views.name: team_attributes_row
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  team_fifa_api_id,
  team_api_id,
  date,
  buildUpPlaySpeed,
  buildUpPlaySpeedClass,
  buildUpPlayPassing,
  buildUpPlayPassingClass,
  buildUpPlayDribbling,
  buildUpPlayDribblingClass,
  chanceCreationPassing,
  chanceCreationCrossing,
  chanceCreationShooting,
  defencePressure,
  defenceAggression,
  defenceTeamWidth,
  defenceDefenderLineClass
FROM Team_Attributes
views.description: One row per Team_Attributes record exposing raw team attribute measures and keys, for filtering cohorts of team attribute snapshots by date or attribute values.

views.name: team_latest_attributes_by_team_api_id
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ta.team_api_id,
  ta.team_fifa_api_id,
  ta.id,
  ta.date,
  ta.buildUpPlaySpeed,
  ta.buildUpPlaySpeedClass,
  ta.buildUpPlayPassing,
  ta.buildUpPlayPassingClass,
  ta.chanceCreationCrossing,
  ta.defencePressure
FROM Team_Attributes AS ta
JOIN (
  SELECT team_api_id, MAX(date) AS max_date
  FROM Team_Attributes
  WHERE team_api_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY team_api_id
) AS latest
  ON ta.team_api_id = latest.team_api_id
  AND ta.date = latest.max_date
views.description: For each team_api_id, pick the latest Team_Attributes snapshot (by date) and expose key attribute measures — useful for questions about current/latest team characteristics.

views.name: team_with_metadata
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Team_Attributes.id AS "Team_Attributes.id",
  Team.team_api_id AS "Team.team_api_id",
  Team.team_fifa_api_id AS "Team.team_fifa_api_id",
  Team.team_long_name AS "Team.team_long_name",
  Team.team_short_name AS "Team.team_short_name",
  Team_Attributes.date AS "Team_Attributes.date",
  Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed AS "Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed",
  Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeedClass AS "Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeedClass"
FROM Team_Attributes
LEFT JOIN Team
  ON Team_Attributes.team_api_id = Team.team_api_id
views.description: Denormalized team metadata joining Team (names/ids) to Team_Attributes snapshots to allow queries that need human-readable team names along with attribute measures.

views.name: team_attributes_annual_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  team_api_id,
  team_fifa_api_id,
  date,
  buildUpPlayPassing
FROM Team_Attributes
WHERE strftime('%Y', date) = '<YEAR_LITERAL>'
views.description: Row-level cohort of Team_Attributes rows filtered to a single calendar year. Keeps original attribute measures and keys; intended as a reusable per-record 1-row-per-Team_Attributes entry cohort for a chosen year.

views.name: team_attributes_per_team_annual_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  team_api_id,
  strftime('%Y', date) AS year,
  COUNT(buildUpPlayPassing) AS count_buildUpPlayPassing,
  SUM(buildUpPlayPassing) AS sum_buildUpPlayPassing,
  AVG(buildUpPlayPassing) AS avg_buildUpPlayPassing,
  MIN(id) AS id -- carry a source id to keep joinable (min id per team/year)
FROM Team_Attributes
WHERE date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY team_api_id, strftime('%Y', date)
views.description: Aggregated measures of Team_Attributes per team_api_id for a chosen year. Produces raw aggregates (SUM, COUNT, AVG) of numeric attributes per team for that year; grain is one row per team_api_id within that year.

views.name: team_join_team_attributes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Team_Attributes.id AS id,
  Team_Attributes.team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  Team.team_long_name AS team_long_name,
  Team_Attributes.date AS date,
  Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassing AS buildUpPlayPassing
FROM Team_Attributes
LEFT JOIN Team
  ON Team_Attributes.team_api_id = Team.team_api_id
views.description: Denormalized join of Team with Team_Attributes (row-level) to expose team_long_name alongside Team_Attributes measures and date. Grain is one row per Team_Attributes.id joined to Team by team_api_id.

views.name: player_attributes_with_player_identity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pa.id AS player_attributes_id,
  COALESCE(pa.player_api_id, p.player_api_id) AS player_api_id,
  COALESCE(pa.player_fifa_api_id, p.player_fifa_api_id) AS player_fifa_api_id,
  p.player_name AS player_name,
  p.birthday AS birthday,
  pa.preferred_foot AS preferred_foot
FROM Player_Attributes pa
LEFT JOIN Player p
  ON (pa.player_api_id IS NOT NULL AND pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id)
  OR (pa.player_fifa_api_id IS NOT NULL AND pa.player_fifa_api_id = p.player_fifa_api_id)
views.description: One row per Player_Attributes row enriched with the canonical Player identity fields (to join attributes to player metadata like birthday and player_api_id). Keeps both player_api_id and player_fifa_api_id from both tables to allow stable joining and deduping.

views.name: players_canonical_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  p.player_fifa_api_id AS player_fifa_api_id,
  p.player_name AS player_name,
  p.birthday AS birthday,
  pa.preferred_foot AS preferred_foot,
  pa.date AS attributes_date,
  p.id AS player_id,
  pa.id AS player_attributes_id
FROM Player p
JOIN Player_Attributes pa
  ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
  -- pick the latest attributes row per player by date
  AND pa.date = (
    SELECT MAX(pa2.date)
    FROM Player_Attributes pa2
    WHERE pa2.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
  )
views.description: One canonical row per player (Player.player_api_id) choosing the latest Player_Attributes snapshot when multiple attribute rows exist. Exposes stable player id, birthday, preferred_foot and the attributes snapshot date so downstream queries can count distinct players or filter by birthday year without double-counting.

views.name: player_birthyear_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  p.birthday AS birthday,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', p.birthday) AS INTEGER) AS birth_year,
  pa.preferred_foot AS preferred_foot
FROM Player p
LEFT JOIN player_attributes_rows pa
  ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.birthday, pa.preferred_foot
views.description: A reusable cohort view that selects players with their birth year extracted and exposes each player once (player_api_id) with birthday and preferred_foot, suitable for age/year range filters and aggregation. Does not aggregate counts — leaves counting to final query.

views.name: player_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_api_id,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  player_name,
  birthday,
  height,
  weight,
  id AS player_id
FROM Player
views.description: One row per player exposing stable player identifiers and basic attributes for filtering and joining (canonical player cohort).

views.name: player_attributes_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  player_api_id,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  date,
  long_shots,
  overall_rating,
  potential,
  preferred_foot
FROM Player_Attributes
views.description: Raw player attributes records (one row per Player_Attributes.id) with attribute measures and the date they were recorded. Keeps NULLs so downstream filters can exclude them as needed.

views.name: player_long_shots_by_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_api_id,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  AVG(long_shots) AS long_shots_avg,
  COUNT(long_shots) AS long_shots_count
FROM Player_Attributes
WHERE long_shots IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY player_api_id, player_fifa_api_id
views.description: Per-player aggregated measures for the long_shots attribute: count of non-null observations and average long_shots. One row per player (identified by player_api_id and player_fifa_api_id).

views.name: player_attributes_heading_measure
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  player_api_id,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  date,
  heading_accuracy
FROM Player_Attributes
WHERE heading_accuracy IS NOT NULL
views.description: Raw Player_Attributes rows normalized for player-level skill measures; exposes heading_accuracy and the keys to join back to Player. Keeps one row per Player_Attributes.id.

views.name: player_heading_accuracy_avg_per_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pa.player_fifa_api_id AS player_fifa_api_id,
  pa.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  AVG(pa.heading_accuracy) AS avg_heading_accuracy,
  COUNT(pa.heading_accuracy) AS heading_record_count
FROM Player_Attributes pa
GROUP BY
  pa.player_fifa_api_id,
  pa.player_api_id
views.description: Average heading_accuracy per player (grouped at player_fifa_api_id and player_api_id) plus count of attribute records to allow excluding players with zero records.

views.name: matches_season_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS match_id,
  m.league_id AS league_id,
  m.season AS season,
  m.home_team_goal AS home_team_goal,
  m.away_team_goal AS away_team_goal,
  m.date AS date
FROM Match m
WHERE m.season IS NOT NULL
views.description: One-row-per-match cohort with season filter metadata exposed. Keeps raw match-level fields needed for season-level analyses (scores, league, teams, date).

views.name: league_match_goal_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.league_id AS league_id,
  m.season AS season,
  COUNT(m.id) AS matches_count,
  AVG(m.home_team_goal) AS avg_home_team_goal,
  AVG(m.away_team_goal) AS avg_away_team_goal
FROM
  matches_with_valid_score_and_season m
GROUP BY
  m.league_id,
  m.season
views.description: Aggregated match-level goal measures per league per season: computes count of matches and average home and away goals. Grouped at league + season so it can be compared across leagues for a given season.

views.name: league_dimension
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  League.id AS league_id,
  League.name AS league_name,
  League.country_id AS country_id
FROM League
views.description: Canonical league dimension exposing league id and name for joins and reporting.

views.name: players_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_api_id,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  player_name,
  birthday,
  height,
  weight
FROM Player
WHERE birthday IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical, cleaned projection of the Player table: one row per player with core identifiers and personal attributes (birthday, height, weight). Keeps raw values and exposes them for downstream filtering (e.g. by year or month of birthday).

views.name: player_attributes_by_player_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pa.id AS player_attributes_id,
  pa.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  pa.player_fifa_api_id AS player_fifa_api_id,
  pa.date AS date,
  pa.overall_rating AS overall_rating,
  pa.potential AS potential,
  pa.preferred_foot AS preferred_foot,
  pa.attacking_work_rate AS attacking_work_rate,
  pa.defensive_work_rate AS defensive_work_rate
FROM Player_Attributes pa
views.description: Player_Attributes rows linked to Player identifiers. One row per Player_Attributes record (player_api_id + date), exposing attribute measures so callers can join player metadata to specific attribute snapshots or filter by attribute date.

views.name: players_birth_ym
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Player.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  Player.player_fifa_api_id AS player_fifa_api_id,
  Player.player_name AS player_name,
  Player.birthday AS birthday,
  substr(Player.birthday, 1, 4) AS birth_year,
  substr(Player.birthday, 6, 2) AS birth_month
FROM Player
WHERE Player.birthday IS NOT NULL
views.description: Extracted year and month components from Player.birthday for easy cohorting by birth year/month. One row per player (player_api_id) with computed birth_year and birth_month as strings matching substr semantics.

views.name: player_attributes_with_player_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pa.id AS id,
  pa.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  p.player_name AS player_name,
  pa.date AS date,
  pa.overall_rating AS overall_rating
FROM Player_Attributes pa
LEFT JOIN Player p
  ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
views.description: Denormalized join of Player_Attributes to Player to provide attribute snapshots together with player_name and player identifiers. One row per Player_Attributes.id (attribute snapshot) with player metadata attached.
counter_examples: What was the overall rating for Aaron Mooy on 2016/2/4?

views.name: matches_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.season AS season,
  m.country_id AS country_id,
  m.home_team_goal AS home_team_goal
FROM Match m
views.description: One-row-per-match cohort exposing match identifiers, season, country linkage, and home team goals (raw), suitable for season- and country-level filtering and final aggregation.

views.name: country_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  name
FROM
  Country
views.description: Canonical country table exposing country id and name for joins/filters by country name.

views.name: match_with_country_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.season AS season,
  c.id AS country_id,
  c.name AS country_name,
  m.home_team_goal AS home_team_goal
FROM Match m
JOIN Country c
  ON m.country_id = c.id
views.description: Denormalized match rows joined to country (country name) to simplify queries that filter matches by country name and season. Keeps raw match measures (home_team_goal) and join keys.

views.name: player_basics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  player_name AS player_name,
  height AS height,
  weight AS weight,
  birthday AS birthday,
  id AS id
FROM Player
views.description: One row per player with canonical basic attributes (id, player_api_id, player_name, birthday, height, weight). Useful as the canonical player dimension/cohort.

views.name: player_attributes_finishing_by_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  AVG(pa.finishing) AS avg_finishing,
  COUNT(pa.finishing) AS cnt_finishing
FROM Player_Attributes pa
JOIN Player p ON p.player_api_id = pa.player_api_id
WHERE pa.finishing IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.player_api_id
views.description: Per-player aggregated finishing stats from Player_Attributes: average finishing and count of finishing observations. One row per Player.player_api_id. Keeps raw measure and support for filtering out players without finishing values.

views.name: tallest_and_shortest_players_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  p.player_name AS player_name,
  p.height AS height,
  CASE WHEN p.height = (SELECT MAX(height) FROM Player) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_tallest,
  CASE WHEN p.height = (SELECT MIN(height) FROM Player) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_shortest
FROM Player p
WHERE p.player_api_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Cohort of players who are either at the maximum height or the minimum height in the Player table. One row per player (player_api_id) with their height and player_name. Useful for questions comparing extreme-height players.

views.name: player_attributes_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pa.id AS id,
  CAST(pa.player_api_id AS INTEGER) AS player_api_id,
  CAST(pa.player_fifa_api_id AS INTEGER) AS player_fifa_api_id,
  pa.date AS date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', pa.date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(pa.overall_rating AS INTEGER) AS overall_rating,
  CAST(pa.potential AS INTEGER) AS potential,
  pa.preferred_foot AS preferred_foot,
  pa.attacking_work_rate AS attacking_work_rate,
  pa.defensive_work_rate AS defensive_work_rate,
  CASE WHEN (p.height IS NULL) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS height_null_flag
FROM Player_Attributes pa
LEFT JOIN Player p
  ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
views.description: Canonical cleaned row-level Player_Attributes records with parsed year and explicit NULL-safe casts for key columns, exposing player and attribute fields useful for cohorts and joins.

views.name: player_attributes_with_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  PA.id AS id,
  PA.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  P.player_name AS player_name,
  PA.date AS date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', PA.date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  PA.overall_rating AS overall_rating,
  P.height AS height
FROM Player_Attributes AS PA
JOIN Player AS P
  ON PA.player_api_id = P.player_api_id
views.description: Denormalized Player_Attributes rows joined to Player core info (one row per Player_Attributes.id) to enable year and player-attribute filters in one relation.

views.name: player_core_46
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_api_id,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  player_name,
  birthday,
  height,
  weight
FROM Player
views.description: One row per player exposing stable player identifiers and basic player attributes (name, birthday, height, weight) for joining and filtering.

views.name: player_attributes_atomic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  player_api_id,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  date,
  ball_control,
  overall_rating,
  potential,
  preferred_foot
FROM Player_Attributes
views.description: Raw player attribute measurements. One row per Player_Attributes record (timestamped measurement) exposing all numeric attribute columns; NULLs preserved so callers can exclude them as needed.

views.name: player_ball_control_avg_by_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pa.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  pa.player_fifa_api_id AS player_fifa_api_id,
  AVG(pa.ball_control) AS avg_ball_control,
  COUNT(pa.ball_control) AS num_samples
FROM Player_Attributes pa
WHERE pa.ball_control IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  pa.player_api_id,
  pa.player_fifa_api_id
views.description: Average ball_control per player (grouped at player_api_id). Excludes NULL ball_control values in the average. Keeps both player_api_id and player_fifa_api_id for join flexibility.

views.name: player_attributes_snapshot
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pa.id AS player_attributes_id,
  pa.player_api_id,
  pa.player_fifa_api_id,
  pa.date,
  pa.overall_rating,
  pa.potential,
  pa.preferred_foot
FROM Player_Attributes pa
JOIN (
  SELECT player_api_id, MAX(date) AS max_date
  FROM Player_Attributes
  GROUP BY player_api_id
) latest
  ON pa.player_api_id = latest.player_api_id
  AND pa.date = latest.max_date
views.description: Latest (most recent date) attributes snapshot per player_api_id from Player_Attributes. Useful for queries needing the most recent overall_rating, potential, preferred_foot, etc.

views.name: player_with_latest_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_api_id,
  p.player_name,
  p.player_fifa_api_id,
  p.birthday,
  p.height,
  p.weight,
  pa.date AS attr_date,
  pa.overall_rating,
  pa.potential,
  pa.preferred_foot,
  p.id AS player_id,
  pa.id AS player_attributes_id
FROM Player p
LEFT JOIN Player_Attributes pa
  ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
  AND pa.date = (
    SELECT MAX(date) FROM Player_Attributes pa2
    WHERE pa2.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
  )
views.description: Denormalized view joining canonical Player rows with their latest Player_Attributes snapshot (if any). One row per player_api_id combining name/birthday with latest attributes for richer comparisons.

views.name: player_height_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_api_id,
  player_name,
  height
FROM
  Player
WHERE
  height IS NOT NULL
views.description: Subset/cohort of Player rows exposing only players with non-null heights and useful identifiers for comparing or grouping by height.

views.description: Row-level player attribute records (one row per Player_Attributes.id) with core attribute columns and identifying player keys. Useful as the base cohort for filtering by preferred foot, work rates, ratings, and time-based selection.
counter_examples: What was the overall rating for Aaron Mooy on 2016/2/4?

views.description: For each player (player_api_id) return the most recent Player_Attributes row by date. Useful when questions ask about players' current/most-recent attributes (one row per player).

views.description: Normalized rows of player attribute snapshots. One row per Player_Attributes.id snapshot, exposing raw attribute columns and canonical keys for joining to Player.

views.name: player_attributes_with_player_55

views.name: match_with_league
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id,
  m.match_api_id,
  l.id AS league_id,
  l.name AS league_name,
  m.date,
  m.season,
  m.home_team_api_id,
  m.away_team_api_id
FROM Match m
LEFT JOIN League l
  ON m.league_id = l.id
views.description: Denormalized match rows joined to their league name to simplify common queries that filter matches by league and date. One row per Match.id with League.id and League.name included.

views.name: player_latest_attributes_61
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pa.player_api_id,
  pa.player_fifa_api_id,
  pa.date,
  pa.overall_rating,
  pa.potential,
  pa.preferred_foot,
  p.height,
  p.weight
FROM Player_Attributes pa
JOIN Player p
  ON p.player_api_id = pa.player_api_id
WHERE pa.id IN (
  SELECT MAX(id) FROM Player_Attributes GROUP BY player_api_id
)
views.description: For each player (by player_api_id) return their most recent Player_Attributes row (latest date) with key rating and attribute columns. This is useful to compare or aggregate players using their latest-known attributes.

views.name: player_latest_overall_rating
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pa.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  pa.overall_rating AS overall_rating,
  pa.date AS date
FROM Player_Attributes pa
JOIN (
  SELECT player_api_id, MAX(date) AS max_date
  FROM Player_Attributes
  WHERE player_api_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY player_api_id
) latest ON pa.player_api_id = latest.player_api_id AND pa.date = latest.max_date
views.description: Latest overall_rating per player_api_id (one row per player) using max(date) from Player_Attributes. Exposes the raw overall_rating value from the most recent attributes row for use in comparisons/ratios.

views.name: player_attributes_rows_63
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  PA.id AS id,
  PA.player_api_id AS player_api_id,

  PA.date AS date,
  PA.overall_rating AS overall_rating
FROM Player_Attributes PA
WHERE PA.overall_rating IS NOT NULL
views.description: Row-level cleaned Player_Attributes records (one row per Player_Attributes.id) exposing raw attribute measures and keys for joining to Player. Filters out rows where overall_rating is NULL to make downstream averages straightforward.

views.name: player_attributes_by_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_api_id,
  COUNT(id) AS num_attribute_records,
  AVG(overall_rating) AS avg_overall_rating,
  MIN(date) AS min_attribute_date,
  MAX(date) AS max_attribute_date
FROM Player_Attributes
WHERE overall_rating IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY player_api_id
views.description: Aggregated attribute measures for each player_api_id: computes count of attribute observations and basic aggregates (AVG overall_rating, MIN/MAX date). Grain is per player_api_id so final queries can join to player metadata to report per-player averages without further grouping.

views.name: team_attributes_with_team
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Team_Attributes.id AS "Team_Attributes.id",
  Team_Attributes.team_api_id AS "Team_Attributes.team_api_id",
  Team_Attributes.team_fifa_api_id AS "Team_Attributes.team_fifa_api_id",
  Team.team_long_name AS "Team.team_long_name",
  Team.team_short_name AS "Team.team_short_name",
  Team_Attributes.date AS "Team_Attributes.date",
  Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassing AS "Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassing",
  Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassingClass AS "Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassingClass"
FROM Team_Attributes
LEFT JOIN Team
  ON (Team.team_api_id IS NOT NULL AND Team.team_api_id = Team_Attributes.team_api_id)
     OR (Team.team_fifa_api_id IS NOT NULL AND Team.team_fifa_api_id = Team_Attributes.team_fifa_api_id)
views.description: Denormalized Team_Attributes rows joined to Team identity using either team_api_id or team_fifa_api_id to allow attribute lookups by team name. Keeps one row per Team_Attributes record and includes team_long_name for easy filtering.

views.name: player_attribute_snapshot_with_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Player_Attributes.id AS id,
  Player.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  Player.player_name AS player_name,
  Player.birthday AS birthday,
  Player_Attributes.date AS date,
  Player_Attributes.overall_rating AS overall_rating
FROM Player_Attributes
JOIN Player
  ON Player_Attributes.player_api_id = Player.player_api_id
views.description: Denormalized join of Player_Attributes snapshot to Player core info. One row per Player_Attributes.id enriched with player_name and birthday to support queries that filter attribute snapshots and then select players ordered by birthdate.
